transcript:
Meeting header:
- Date/Time: 2026-03-30 16:15 UTC
- Duration: 58 minutes
- Attendees: Sofia (Redwood AE), Marco (Redwood SE), Priya (Redwood SE), Daniel (CTO), Maya (ML Eng), Carlos (SRE), Olivia (Security)

Summary (auto): quick discovery to map exit path from OpenAI + vLLM/TGI internal stack, discuss parity and security gating.

[00:00] Sofia Kim: Hey everyone thanks for joining, we'll keep this to an hour. quick intros?
[00:08] Daniel Park: Hi Daniel here, CTO at LumenForge, I'm joined by Maya (ML eng) and Carlos (SRE), Olivia is on security. We're evaluating moving some models off OpenAI due to cost and data residency.
[00:20] Maya Singh: Yeah mostly for high-churn synth tasks, we run TGI and vLLM internally for some endpoints now, we also use OpenAI for others cause of latency and dev speed.
[00:35] Marco Alvarez: Cool, thanks. Can you sketch the main constraints—latency targets, seq lengths, throughput?
[00:42] Carlos Rivera: 95% under 250ms for small chat flows, but for the large batch text-gen we can tolerate up to 1.5s. seq lengths average 512 tokens but spikes to 2k for research queries.
[00:55] Olivia Chen: From security side: SOC2 is required, keys in our KMS (we cannot pass plaintext keys to third party), and data residency: EU and US segments, finance data must stay in EU region. Also need audit logs retained 1 year.
[01:12] Priya Nair: Noted. Redwood Private supports customer-managed KMS and VPC deployments — we've done on-prem pockets for regulated customers. Quick Q: are you looking for immediate lift-and-shift parity or staged migration?
[01:24] Daniel Park: staged. We want a hosted quick win for non-sensitive flows, and then Dedicated/Private for regulated pipelines. But must verify eval parity: outputs from TGI/vLLM vs Redwood-hosted models — we need minimal drift.
[01:38] Maya Singh: Right, we've tuned TGI with custom tokens and rx embedding tweaks; concerned about rerank and reranking parity too.
[01:45] Marco Alvarez: On parity we usually run evals side-by-side. we can ingest your prompt sets, run them across the candidate models (both Redwood hosted and dedicated variants), capture diffs on n-gram, semantic similarity, and confidence. Also track latency tail and token cost.
[02:02] Daniel Park: How do you handle KV cache / long context? our vLLM+TGI stack has custom kv caching and offload patterns to keep tails down.
[02:12] Marco Alvarez: Redwood runtime has KV cache management and prefix caching. It's not one-to-one with a custom vLLM tweak but we expose policies for cache TTL and shard placement. there might be small behavior diffs on incremental decoding if you've made custom kernel patches.
[02:28] Maya Singh: Any gotchas moving from OpenAI API? e.g., function calling or tool calls mapping?
[02:34] Priya Nair: We support function/tool calling semantics and structured outputs, but the exact schema mapping may need small adapter layers. some of our customers write thin translators to keep app code stable.
[02:47] Carlos Rivera: On infra—if we go Dedicated, what GPU types are typical? we run mixed workloads and want predictable throughput.
[02:56] Marco Alvarez: Common choices are A100/4090-class or next gen L4 for cheaper throughput. we provide reserved pools and autoscaling; you can pin model variants to specific hardware for consistent latency.
[03:12] Olivia Chen: Encryption in transit and at rest? and do you integrate with customer KMS like AWS KMS or Hashicorp Vault?
[03:20] Priya Nair: Yes TLS + at rest encryption. For Private we integrate with customer KMS/HSM — we've done AWS KMS and Google KMS and Hashicorp. For hosted we offer envelope encryption but for the strictest customers we recommend Private with KMS.
[03:33] Daniel Park: Pricing—our spend with OpenAI is significant. Can you give ballpark for token unit and dedicated commitments?
[03:40] Sofia Kim: we'll send a delta sheet but in general hosted is competitive vs OpenAI for token price at volume; Dedicated includes a fixed monthly for reserved capacity plus lower per-token compute. we'll send three example configs.
[03:55] Maya Singh: Benchmarks: we need a run that mirrors our traffic shape — spikey 500-700 rps for small prompts + long research batches overnight. can Redwood simulate that?
[04:06] Marco Alvarez: absolutely — we ask for a test harness (or we can provide one) with your seq length distribution and arrival patterns. Marco: we'll also run vLLM/TGI locally to make apples-to-apples comparisons.
[04:22] Daniel Park: What about model variants? we tuned LlamaX and an in-house quantized model on vLLM. Can Redwood host customer models?
[04:31] Priya Nair: Yes we onboard custom models; for Dedicated/Private you can bring custom weights and we support quantized formats and common runtimes. For hosted we currently curate open models but can discuss private model hosting under enterprise contracts.
[04:47] Olivia Chen: Auditability—can you surface per-request logs, token-level cost, and redaction controls?
[04:54] Marco Alvarez: Yes, Redwood Console shows token-level breakdowns, per-route dashboards, and you can configure PII redaction rules; logs can be exported to your SIEM.
[05:06] Daniel Park: Any migration risks we should plan for?
[05:09] Sofia Kim: Typical risks: eval drift, slight latency regressions if kernel-level optimizations differ, and integration work for KMS/SSO. Mitigations: side-by-side evals, canary rollout with fallback to OpenAI, and a scoped POC.
[05:23] Carlos Rivera: Canary and fallback—how fast is fallback?
[05:26] Marco Alvarez: Policy-based routing can detect high error or latency and failover within seconds depending on health checks; you can set fallback tiers (hosted -> dedicated -> openai remote).
[05:36] Maya Singh: For eval parity what metrics do you report? we care about BLEU-ish, embedding cosine, hallucination rate, and latency p99.
[05:44] Priya Nair: We'll capture n-gram overlap, semantic similarity via embeddings, perplexity where possible, hallucination heuristics, and latency percentiles p50/p95/p99 — we'll generate a parity report.
[05:55] Daniel Park: Timeline—if we like the results, we want a pilot in 6 weeks. Is that reasonable?
[06:00] Sofia Kim: Yes, pilot in that window is doable. Next steps: share security pack, send pricing, get your eval prompts, and schedule benchmark.
[06:12] Olivia Chen: I'll confirm KMS vendor and data residency constraints, expect a note by end of week.
[06:18] Sofia Kim: Great. any final Qs?
[06:20] Maya Singh: One small thing—does Redwood support server-side caching for repeated prefixes to reduce cost?
[06:26] Marco Alvarez: Yes that's the prefix/KV caching I mentioned; we can tune TTL and cache hit behavior. sometimes user-level dedupe logic sits in front too.
[06:36] Daniel Park: Thanks all. we'll review and pick dates for benchmark.
[06:40] Sofia Kim: Thanks team, we'll follow up with the pack and proposed times.

Meeting end.
questions: Can Redwood simulate LumenForge traffic pattern for benchmarks?
How do you manage KMS integrations for Hosted vs Private?
What metrics define 'eval parity' vs our TGI outputs?
What's the expected timeline for a pilot?
